official.deadline_note: The 2027 cycle has an earlier eligibility gate and an earlier reference deadline: the eligibility confirmation request is due October 2, 2026; references must be received by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET (a week before the application deadline); mandatory information sessions are held in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027 Scholarship competition - application period September 1 to November 6, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. (ET)
official.status_note: The Foundation states the application period for the 2027 Scholarship runs from September 1 to November 6, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. (ET), and that the complete application is due November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. (ET).
official.tuition_coverage_note: The official scholarship page states the annual stipend of up to $50,000 is 'To cover tuition and living expenses related to your doctoral studies.'
benefits: An annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses
An annual allowance of up to $20,000 for three years to support research, networking activities, and travel related to doctoral work and Foundation programming
Mentorship and experiential learning through meetings, masterclasses, seminars, and field experiences with Mentors, Fellows and Scholars
Membership in an engaged multidisciplinary community and lifelong membership in the Foundation's alumni network of more than 500 individuals
Part-time work of up to 20 hours per week permitted while receiving full scholarship benefits
eligibility: At the time of application, be in the first year or the second year of a PhD program
Field of study broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and addressing issues relevant to Canada's future
PhD research must align with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment

Eligible applicants are: a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university; a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada; or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university
International students residing outside Canada or enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible
Three letters of reference required: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, one from a referee outside academia
Applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and a high level of intellectual ability
requirements: Complete the eligibility screening form first; only applicants whose eligibility is confirmed by the Foundation can access the full application form
Applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed

Declare all additional sources of income each year, including other scholarships, as the scholarship value is adjusted based on amounts received from other organizations, institutions, or universities
Exactly three referees required - no more, no less; family members are not permitted as referees
documents: Eligibility verification/screening form submitted via the Foundation's SmartSimple portal
Complete 2027 Scholarship application form, filled out in English or French (one language only)
Three letters of reference: PhD supervisor, another academic referee, and a non-academic referee
Transcripts, assessed as part of the entire application
selection_criteria: Academic excellence, supported by an outstanding academic record
Clear alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and its four founding themes
Ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society
Intellectual curiosity, ambition, leadership potential, commitment to society, and desire to create meaningful impact beyond academia
Willingness to engage in dialogue, interdisciplinary collaboration, and knowledge sharing
coverage: Up to $50,000 per year for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Up to $20,000 per year for three years to support research, networking activities, and travel related to doctoral work
Registration for Foundation programming, including meetings, masterclasses, seminars, and field experiences
application_method: Step 1: complete the eligibility screening form at fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca (opened September 1, 2026)
Step 2: once the Foundation confirms eligibility, access and complete the full 2027 Scholarship application form through the portal
Step 3: referees submit their three letters through the application file; the application cannot be submitted unless all reference letters are attached
official.application_route: Two-step online application via the Foundation's SmartSimple portal: first the eligibility screening form, then the full 2027 application form once eligibility is confirmed.
official.study_mode: Full-time doctoral enrolment (Foundation programming participation expected); part-time work of up to 20 hours per week is permitted
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian students may be enrolled at a Canadian university or at a university outside Canada; international students must be enrolled at a Canadian university; international students residing outside Canada or enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students enrolled in a doctoral program at a Canadian university are eligible; those residing outside Canada or enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Doctoral research broadly related to the humanities or social sciences that addresses issues relevant to Canada's future and aligns with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment
official.research_requirement: A compelling research project aligned with at least one of the Foundation's four founding themes; the rigour of the research proposal is assessed, and shortlisted candidates are invited to group meetings and individual interviews
official.description: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship supports doctoral students with an excellent academic record who are engaged in humanities and social sciences research that contributes to the advancement of Canada and society. The Foundation frames it as more than financial support: Scholars receive an annual stipend and an annual research and travel allowance, join mentorship and experiential learning programming, and become part of a multidisciplinary community of more than 500 alumni.
official.region: Canada (Canadian students may also study abroad)
official.english_requirement: No IELTS or TOEFL score is published. The Foundation states applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English - fluency in both official languages is not required - and the application form may be completed in either official language (one language only).

applicant_utility.summary: This is one of Canada's most substantial doctoral awards: up to $50,000 a year for three years explicitly aimed at tuition and living costs, plus up to $20,000 a year for research, networking, and travel. The catch is the gate: you cannot open the full application until the Foundation confirms your eligibility through the short screening form, and that confirmation request closes October 2, 2026 - well before the November 6 application deadline. Plan around the three required referees, including one who knows you from outside academia, because your file cannot be submitted without all three letters attached.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First- or second-year humanities and social sciences PhD students at a Canadian university, or Canadian students anywhere in the world, whose research maps clearly onto one of the Foundation's four founding themes and who can show engagement beyond the academy.
application_readiness_checklist: Map your project explicitly to one of the four themes (Human Rights and Dignity, Responsible Citizenship, Canada and the World, People and their Natural Environment) before writing anything, and use that mapping as the spine of the proposal
Submit the eligibility screening form early in the September 1 to October 2 window rather than in the final days, so any correction request does not lock you out of the full form
Secure your three referees (supervisor, academic, non-academic) the moment eligibility is confirmed - references are due October 30, a full week before the application deadline
If your supervisor is new or does not know your work well, use a former supervisor and explain the situation in the Special Circumstances section as the Foundation recommends
Attend one of the mandatory information sessions in the weeks of October 5 or October 12, 2026
Choose English or French for the whole application before you start, and check that your thesis is not already committed to a different funding deadline in the same window
common_rejection_risks: Skipping or misreading the two-step process: the screening form only confirms your eligibility, it does not apply for you, and applicants whose eligibility is not confirmed never see the full form
Research that is genuinely strong but framed in disciplinary terms with no visible line to one of the four founding themes, which is the single clearest published alignment criterion

A third referee who is actually an academic colleague or a family member, when the requirement is specifically someone who knows you outside academia; exactly three referees are accepted, no more and no fewer
Leaving references until application week and missing the October 30 deadline - a file with an unattached letter simply cannot be submitted
Mixing languages: the form must be completed in one official language only, and referees may write in either, so decide early and keep referees informed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is published as 'up to' $50,000 a year and is reduced by other declared scholarships, with a guaranteed floor of $25,000 for the stipend plus the $20,000 allowance. At universities with high doctoral tuition the stipend may not stretch to cover everything, and the official pages name no funding for relocation, dependants, or incidental living costs, so budget for those separately. Scholars are not Foundation employees and receive no paid parental leave, and payments pause during a leave of absence of up to one year until full-time enrolment resumes.
document_audit: Exactly three reference letters, one from each required referee category; family members are disqualified, and letters must be uploaded into the application file rather than emailed separately to the Foundation
Referees may write in French or English regardless of the language of your application - tell them explicitly which language you chose so nothing is lost
The application must be completed in a single language; switching mid-form is not possible, so freeze the language choice first
A confirmation email is your only receipt: the portal deletes applications once the competition closes, so keep screenshots of the submission and correspondence
alerts: The 2027 cycle closes November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET, but the eligibility request deadline (October 2) and the reference deadline (October 30, 9:00 a.m. ET) fall far earlier - treat October 2 as the real deadline
Information sessions in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026 are mandatory for 2027 applicants
The award value is adjusted against other scholarships and must be declared annually, so model your full funding package before accepting a competing offer
Interviews and group meetings are held in the applicant's preferred official language, and shortlisted candidates travel to Montreal for the interview
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Eligibility screening form in SmartSimple first, Foundation confirmation, then the full application form with three reference letters uploaded by October 30 and the complete package submitted by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
